svg.title: Native Mac development: shared debug build and explicit review
svg.desc: Native source changes first resolve a supported physical Mac architecture, process architecture, Rosetta state and Rust host. The scoped agent Cargo wrapper uses the locked dependency graph and shared target/agents debug cache while protecting the user target/debug directory. The native candidate helper resolves the executable from successful Cargo artifact output and packages a complete Fleetworks.app with resources, Info.plist, architecture checks, hashes, manifest and printed output path. Launch occurs only with an explicit open request on matching physical hardware. Selected Runtime fixtures use the same production views with synthetic effects and require inspection of generated PNG and accessibility output. Fixture evidence and packaging are separate from observed GUI behavior. These helpers start no backend, initialize no user workspace and perform no configuration reset. External backend and web provisioning, Venture and retained terminal compatibility tools remain separate operations.
svg.text: NATIVE CLIENT · ONE HOST DEBUG GRAPH AND ONE BUILD OWNER
Select affected checks and fixture scenes
Physical CPU / process CPU / Rust host
Resolve Rosetta or host mismatch first
Reuse target/agents and the same graph
Print the exact app and artifact paths
Only --open, on the matching physical Mac
Keep package and GUI results distinct
Backend and web provisioning are independent operator work
The app connects to an authorized configured gateway. This host loop starts no Docker, database, index, inference or web relay.
Venture and terminal clients remain compatibility tools. Preserve existing stacks, data, images and user configuration.
Repeat only the affected work. Neither a complete package nor an offline fixture proves installed GUI or live backend behavior.
